answer: A falcon-style reputation check works like this: every agent must stake a refundable deposit before it can act as a bridge between two markets, and a public beacon ledger records each agent's successful deliveries. A newcomer with no history can only handle tiny trades until it builds a record, while creating a fake identity costs a fresh deposit plus weeks of small honest work. An attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents would need a thousand deposits and a thousand slow histories, so the cost of forging a crowd exceeds the profit from gaming one trade.
